words: Person guiding concertgoers to their seats
Place for one person to sit
Line of things side by side
Passage between rows of seats or shelves
Fabric panel hung at a window
Printed guide to a performance or event
Entrance area outside a concert auditorium
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Applaud by striking the hands together
Performer who portrays a character in a movie

answerNotes.TICKET: A ticket can give admission or identify an item left for a service. A theater ticket and a dry-cleaning claim ticket serve different uses.
answerNotes.USHER: An usher helps people find seats. The role differs from the performers on stage or the clerk selling tickets.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.AISLE: An aisle is a passage between rows. In a theater it lets people reach seats without climbing over them.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Marked strip of pool space used by a swimmer
Small secure cupboard for personal items
One eyepiece in a swimmer's protective pair
Rest on top of water rather than sink
Walking area around a swimming pool
Opposite of deep when describing water

answerNotes.POOL: Pool can name swimming water or a small area collected in a hollow. A tide pool remains among shore rocks as the sea level falls.
answerNotes.SWIM: Swimming uses the body to move through water. Floating means remaining supported at the surface without necessarily traveling.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.LOCKER: A locker is a small storage compartment that can be secured. It holds belongings while a visitor uses a pool or activity room.
answerNotes.DECK: Deck can mean a pack of playing cards or an outdoor platform. Cards and a patio use different senses of the same short word.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.SHALLOW: Shallow means not deep. At a pool, the word describes the water's depth rather than its temperature.

answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.COFFEE: Coffee is brewed from roasted beans. The familiar beans are actually seeds from the coffee plant's fruit.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.

words: Small piece of ground used for gardening
Area where flowers or vegetables are grown
Prepared section of ground for growing plants
Small building for storing garden tools
Public board with words or symbols
Implement used to do a task

answerNotes.GARDEN: A garden is an area cultivated for plants. A single bed or plot can be one part of a larger garden.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.SHED: A shed is a small storage building. In a garden scene, it may hold tools and supplies rather than livestock.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.TOOL: A tool is an implement used to do a job. The clue may describe its action, such as cutting, turning, or gripping.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.SOIL: Soil is the material around garden roots. It contains more than loose mineral particles: air, water, and decaying material are also part of it.
answerNotes.FENCE: A fence marks a boundary or encloses an area. The gate is its movable entrance rather than another name for the whole barrier.
answerNotes.GATE: A gate opens through a fence or other boundary. Hinges let it move, and a latch holds it closed.

answerNotes.SHELTER: A bus shelter protects waiting passengers from some weather. It does not replace checking the route or arrival information.
answerNotes.BUS: A bus carries several passengers on roads. Its route tells where it goes, while its timetable tells when it is scheduled.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.ROUTE: A route is a planned course. Several roads or stops can be parts of a single route.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.STOP: Stop asks for movement to end. At a crossing, it concerns waiting for the appropriate signal rather than a kind of destination.
answerNotes.FARE: Fare is the price of a journey. A ticket is the record or pass obtained when that fare is paid.
